title: Many coded pictures in one HEIF item can exhaust CPU
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The decoder processed every coded picture in an item or sequence sample even though it returns one image. A 16 kB file with 1,000 hidden HEVC pictures of 4096×4096 reportedly took 14 seconds.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-9W6QJITH. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Decoding now refuses more than eight coded pictures per decode by default. The v1.24.x limit can be configured; zero disables it. Fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.
